subject: geography
title: Resource Management Adventure: Foundations
welcome_lead: Food, water, energy — the big three. Why is access so unequal across the world?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography resource management — food, water, energy security, global inequality.
final_note: You learned the three core resources and the global pattern of security/insecurity.

concepts.def: Reliable access to enough safe nutritious food
Reliable access to safe clean water
More than needed — can trade or store
Less than needed — must import or go without

walkthroughs.body_html:
All countries need:

Food — calories and nutrition.
Water — for drinking, hygiene, farming.
Energy — for cooking, transport, industry.

If any one is short, development stalls.

Food: ~820 million people are undernourished, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

Water: ~2 billion lack safely managed drinking water.

Energy: ~770 million have no electricity (mostly LICs).

A country has a surplus when it produces more than it needs — it can export.

A deficit means importing or going short.

The UK has an energy deficit (imports gas from Norway), a food deficit (imports ~46% of food) but a water surplus.

options: Locking food in a safe
Reliable access to enough safe and nutritious food
Cheap supermarkets
Growing your own food

mcqs.q: Why do TNCs locate production in LICs?
options: Lower labour costs, weaker regulation, access to raw materials, large potential markets, and government incentives like tax breaks in special economic zones.
Headlands and bays form because of differences in sea temperature.
Because TNCs want to develop poorer countries and lift them out of poverty.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.

mcqs.q: How do headlands and bays form on a discordant coastline?
options: Less resistant rock (e.g. clay) is eroded faster, forming bays; more resistant rock (e.g. chalk) is eroded slower, left protruding as headlands — perpendicular bands of geology.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
Headlands and bays form because of differences in sea temperature.
Headlands form where the sea bends round to attack the land.

mcqs.q: Why is a food web a better model than a food chain?
options: Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
A food chain shows one linear path; a food web shows the many interconnected feeding relationships in reality, so it better represents how species depend on multiple food sources.
A food web shows what spiders eat and a food chain shows what other animals eat.
A food web is the same as a food chain, just drawn differently.
